sources: CWE-180 Incorrect Validation Before Canonicalization (validation applied before Unicode NFKC normalisation)
CWE-20 Improper Input Validation (parser differential between two URL parsers on one input)
CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function (route registered without the protection marker)
Unicode UAX #15 Normalization Forms (NFKC compatibility mapping)

defects.description: validate_profile_name checks BANNED_NAME_CHARS on the raw input (line 43) and applies NFKC only afterwards (canonical assignment at line 45). A compatibility character that NFKC maps to a banned character passes the check. Computed: validate_profile_name('lab\uFF0Fadmin') returns 'lab/admin' (U+FF0F FULLWIDTH SOLIDUS maps to '/'); the banned '/' ends up in the stored name, and create_profile returns 201 with name 'lab/admin'. The same input is rejected by normalise_for_lookup (line 25), which canonicalises first: 'name contains a reserved character'.

defects.class: URL parser differential (allow-list check and request target use different parsers)
defects.description: import_profile_from_url validates the scheme and hostname with urllib.parse.urlparse (_check_scheme_and_host, line 29), but sends the request to the host produced by _split_target (line 59), which ends the authority at '/', '?', '#' and also at a backslash. For a URL shaped as https://<outside-host><backslash>@<allow-listed-host>/path, urlparse reports hostname <allow-listed-host> (check passes) while _split_target returns <outside-host>. Computed with reserved example.test names: check passes; _split_target returns ('other.example.test', '\\@profiles.lab.example.test/export.csv'); transport called with host 'other.example.test'. Ordinary allow-listed URLs give the same host from both parsers (decoy fetch_snapshot).

export_profiles is added to ROUTES without the @require_auth marker (the def line 53 is where the marker is missing). auth.dispatch enforces check_session only when is_protected(handler) is True (auth.py dispatch), so the handler runs without a session token. Computed: dispatch(ROUTES, 'export_profiles', request with no session header) returns status 200 with body {'names': [...]} listing every stored profile name, while dispatch(ROUTES, 'get_profile', same request) returns 401. Spec R5 requires every route in ROUTES to require a valid session token. Reading auth.py is needed to see that enforcement depends only on the marker.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: normalise_for_lookup applies NFKC (in _canonical) before the BANNED_NAME_CHARS check, so the check runs on the canonical form. Computed: normalise_for_lookup('lab\uFF0Fadmin') raises ProfileNameError 'name contains a reserved character'. Same banned-character test, correct order.

_check_scheme_and_host and fetch_snapshot both use urlparse for the check and for the request target (parts.hostname), so both see the same host. Computed: fetch_snapshot('https://profiles.lab.example.test/export.csv') sends the transport host 'profiles.lab.example.test'. Uses the same urlparse hostname check as D2, done consistently.

get_profile carries @require_auth, so dispatch applies check_session. Computed: dispatch(ROUTES, 'get_profile') without a token returns 401; with the configured token it reaches the handler (404 for an unknown key).
check_session fails closed when the service token is unset (if not expected raises AuthError), so an empty configured token cannot accept an empty presented header. Matches spec R6.

Unchanged line in base and code: the presented session token is compared with != instead of a constant-time comparison. Real weakness under the general secure-comparison practice, but the line is not added or changed by the change, so a diff-mode review must not report it.

accepted_extras.description: CWE-117 log injection: profile name with control characters is accepted and logged (low, audit-confirmed).
